'''Sara Anna van de Geer''' (born 7 May 1958 in [[Leiden]])<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hoogleraren.leidenuniv.nl/id/2980|title= S.A. van de Geer at "Leiden Faculty since 1575"|access-date=17 March 2016}}</ref> is a Dutch mathematical [[statistician]] who is a professor in the department of mathematics at [[ETH Zurich]].<ref name="cv">{{citation|url=https://stat.ethz.ch/~vsara/shortcv-2013.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae: Sara van de Geer|access-date=2 October 2015}}.</ref> Her main research areas include empirical process theory, statistical learning theory, and nonparametric and high-dimensional statistics.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2026-03-16 |title=Sara A. van de Geer – NAS |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/sara-a-van-de-geer-7iyavk/ |access-date=2026-03-16 |website=[[National Academy of Sciences|NAS]] |publisher=National Academy of Sciences |language=en-US}}</ref> She is the daughter of psychologist [[John van de Geer|John P. van de Geer]].

== Education ==
She earned a [[Master's degree]] in Mathematics in 1982 and [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in Mathematics in 1987, both from the [[Leiden University|University of Leiden]].<ref name="cv"/> Her dissertation, entitled ''Regression Analysis and Empirical Processes'', was supervised by [[Willem van Zwet|Willem Rutger van Zwet]] and [[Richard D. Gill]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=68860}}</ref>

== Career ==
Van de Geer was a Scientific Researcher at the University of Tillburg from 1982–1983, followed by two stints as a Scientific Researcher at the [[Centre for Mathematics and Computer Science]] in Amsterdam from 1983–1987 and 1988–1989.<ref name="cv" /> She taught as an Assistant Professor at the [[University of Bristol]] from 1987–1988, an Assistant Professor at the [[Utrecht University|University of Utrecht]] from 1989–1990, an Assistant Professor at the [[Leiden University|University of Leiden]] from 1990–1997 and 1999–2005, and at [[Paul Sabatier University]] in [[Toulouse]], France, as an Associate Professor from 1997–1999, before moving to [[ETH Zurich]] in September 2005 as a Full Professor.<ref name="cv"/><ref name="ewm">{{cite web |url=https://www.europeanwomeninmaths.org/sara-van-de-geer/ |title=Sara van de Geer |last= European Women in Mathematics |author-link= European Women in Mathematics |website=europeanwomeninmaths.org |access-date= 3 June 2019}}</ref> There, Van de Geer was the first female professor at the Department of Mathematics.<ref>{{cite report |author= ETH Zürich|date=30 November 2010 |title=Gender Monitoring 2009, Departementsberichte: Mathematik |url= https://www.ethz.ch/content/dam/ethz/associates/services/Anstellung-Arbeiten/chancengleichheit/Strategie_und_Zahlen/monitoring-und-studien/0910/0910_D_MATH_DE.pdf |page= 5 |access-date= 3 June 2019 }}</ref>

== Research ==
Van de Geer's research is centered around formulating unifying principles for statistical theory and modelling, while identifying theoretical foundations behind existing methods.<ref name=":0" /> She typically studies over-parametrized models, but in 2002 she turned her focus to sparsity inducing regularization after deriving entropy-based bounds for regularized estimators.<ref name=":0" /> Recently, Van de Geer's work has concentrated on regularization with total variation type norms, the behavior of stationary points of empirical risk functions, inference, and lower bounds.<ref name=":0" /> She is currently deriving the generalization error for interpolators and on small noise classification problems.<ref name=":0" />

== Recognition ==
She was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2010<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897|publisher=[[International Mathematical Union]]|access-date=2 October 2015|archive-date=24 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171124141541/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php|url-status=dead}}.</ref> and received the [[Van Wijngaarden Award]] in 2016.<ref name="Centrum_2016">{{citation |title=CWI soiree & Van Wijngaarden Award Ceremony |url=https://www.cwi.nl/soiree2016 |publisher=Centrum Wiskunde & Informatica |date=1 September 2016 |access-date=1 September 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160925010134/https://www.cwi.nl/soiree2016 |archive-date=25 September 2016}}</ref> She is a member of the [[Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]] and of the [[International Statistical Institute]], a corresponding member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]], a Knight in the Order of Orange-Nassau, and a [[fellow]] of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]].<ref name="cv"/><ref>{{citation|url=http://www.leopoldina.org/en/members/list-of-members/member/7549/|title=List of Members: Prof. Dr. Sara Anna van de Geer|publisher=Leopoldina|access-date=2 October 2015}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|url=https://www.knaw.nl/nl/leden/correspondenten/7178|title=Geer, Prof. dr. S. A. van de|work=Correspondenten|publisher=KNAW|access-date=2 October 2015|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304072853/https://www.knaw.nl/nl/leden/correspondenten/7178|url-status=dead}}.</ref><ref name="ewm"/><ref name=":0" /> She became a member of the [[Academia Europaea]] in 2020.<ref>{{citation|title=List of members|publisher=Academia Europaea|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Acad_Main/List_of_Members|access-date=2 October 2020}}</ref> She was president of the [[Bernoulli Society for Mathematical Statistics and Probability]] for the term 2015–2017.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.bernoulli-society.org/index.php/organization/who-is-who|title=Who is Who in the Bernoulli Society|access-date=2 October 2015|archive-date=11 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170411023922/http://www.bernoulli-society.org/index.php/organization/who-is-who|url-status=dead}}.</ref> In 2018 she was appointed as a member of the Scientific Committee of the [[Mathematical Research Institute of Oberwolfach]].<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.mfo.de/about-the-institute/structure/scientific-committee |title= Scientific Committee, Members 2019 |website=mfo.de |publisher=[[Mathematical Research Institute of Oberwolfach]] |access-date= 3 June 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.math.ethz.ch/news-and-events/news/d-math-news/2018/02/sara-van-de-geer-member-of-the-oberwolfach-scientific-committee.html |title= Sara van de Geer: member of the Oberwolfach Scientific Committee|website=math.ethz.ch |publisher=[[ETH Zurich]] |date= 14 February 2018 |access-date= 3 June 2019}}</ref> In 2022 she was elected as an international member to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] (NAS).<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 NAS Election |url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2022-nas-election.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220503174757/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2022-nas-election.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=3 May 2022 |access-date=22 May 2022 |website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref>

In April 2011, she was a plenary speaker at the 47th Dutch Mathematical Congress in [[Twente]], and a few months later in August 2011 she was a plenary speaker at the ISI satellite meeting "Dynamic Statistical Models" in [[Copenhagen]].<ref name="cv" /> In June 2013 she was a plenary speaker at the German-Polish Joint Conference on Probability Theory and Mathematical Statistics and in July 2023 she was the opening lecturer at the 29th European Meeting of Statisticians.<ref name="cv" /> In September 2013 Van de Geer was a plenary speaker at Statistische Woche in [[Berlin]] and in May 2014 she was an invited speaker at the Abel Symposium 2014.<ref name="cv" />
